turns.learner: Hello teacher. I want to practise talking about things around me, like my room. I have a table and a chair in my room.
turns.tutor:
Hello! "I have a table and a chair" is good. We use a for the first mention of a thing.
When we speak about the same thing again, we use the.
Example: I have a dog. The dog is brown.
Now you try. Write two short sentences about your table. First sentence: say you have it. Second sentence: say something about it.

turns.learner: I have a table. A table is big and brown.
turns.tutor:
"I have a table" is good. Your second sentence is nearly right.
Look at the first word of "A table is big and brown." You spoke about the table in sentence one already.
Look at that first word again. Write the second sentence one more time.

turns.learner: I look again. I think A table is correct, because it is a table. It is one table.
turns.tutor:
You are right that it is one table. But "A table" is for the first mention only, not for the second mention of the same table.
Sentence two is the second mention. Change its first word.
Write the second sentence again.

turns.learner: Maybe An table is big and brown? I am not sure about this.
turns.tutor:
Good, you changed the first word. But "An table" is not right: we use an before a vowel sound, and table starts with t.
The second mention needs a different small word. Look at the sentences about my dog again.
Write the second sentence once more.

turns.learner: Ah, I see the dog sentences. The table is big and brown. Is this right, teacher?
turns.tutor:
Yes, "The table is big and brown." is right. Well done.
First mention: "I have a table."
Second mention: "The table is big and brown."
Tell me the rule in your own words.

turns.learner: First time I say a table. Second time I say the table. Same thing again, we use the.
turns.tutor:
Remember: "First time I say a table. Second time I say the table." That is a clear rule.
Now try this one.
Write a or an: I see ___ ant on the table.
